questions.stem: A point at \((2, 3)\) is translated 4 units right and 1 unit down. What are its new coordinates?
questions.hint: Moving right increases the \(x\)-coordinate; moving down decreases the \(y\)-coordinate.

steps.explain: Combine to state the new coordinates.

questions.stem: Point \(A(2, 5)\) is reflected in the \(y\)-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.hint: A reflection in the \(y\)-axis flips the sign of the \(x\)-coordinate only.

steps.explain: Reflecting in the \(y\)-axis negates the \(x\)-coordinate and keeps \(y\) the same.

questions.stem: A rectangle measuring \(3\text{ cm}\) by \(4\text{ cm}\) is enlarged by a scale factor of \(2\). What are the new dimensions?
questions.hint: Multiply each side length by the scale factor.

steps.explain: Multiply both dimensions by the scale factor, 2.

questions.stem: A shape has an area of \(12\text{ cm}^2\). It is enlarged by a scale factor of \(3\). What is the area of the enlarged shape?
questions.hint: When lengths are scaled by a factor \(k\), area is scaled by \(k^2\), not just \(k\).

steps.explain: Area scales by the square of the length scale factor.
Multiply the original area by this factor.
